questions.question: What is the rate-determining step in the electrophilic addition of HBr to propene?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the H-Br bond by light.

options.label: B
options.text: Deprotonation of the alkyl halide by water.

options.label: C
options.text: Protonation of the alkene π bond by HBr to generate the secondary carbocation intermediate: Rate = k[Alkene][HBr].

options.label: D
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of bromide on the secondary carbocation.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of the alkene π bond by HBr to generate the secondary carbocation intermediate: Rate = k[Alkene][HBr].
questions.explanation: Breaking the alkene π bond to form a high-energy carbocation intermediate is endothermic and represents the rate-determining step.

questions.question: Why does electrophilic addition of HCl to 2-methylpropene yield tert-butyl chloride exclusively?

options.label: A
options.text: Protonation at the less substituted =CH₂ carbon yields a tertiary carbocation stabilized by 9 hyperconjugative C-H σ interactions, lowering the transition state energy.

options.label: B
options.text: Protonation at C2 produces a primary carbocation with less steric clash.

options.label: C
options.text: tert-Butyl chloride is an antiaromatic product.

options.label: D
options.text: Chlorine attacks first to form a cyclic chloronium ion.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation at the less substituted =CH₂ carbon yields a tertiary carbocation stabilized by 9 hyperconjugative C-H σ interactions, lowering the transition state energy.
questions.explanation: Hyperconjugation and inductive donation from three methyl groups heavily stabilize the 3° carbocation transition state.

questions.question: What is the key mechanistic intermediate in the bromination of cyclohexene in non-nucleophilic solvent?

options.label: A
options.text: A bridged, cyclic bromonium ion intermediate [C₆H₁₀Br⁺] with positive charge shared across both carbons and bromine.

options.label: B
options.text: A planar open secondary carbocation.

options.label: C
options.text: A 4-membered cyclic bromate ester.

options.label: D
options.text: A free bromine radical pair.

questions.correct_answer: A bridged, cyclic bromonium ion intermediate [C₆H₁₀Br⁺] with positive charge shared across both carbons and bromine.
questions.explanation: Bromine donates a lone pair to the developing positive center during addition, forming a 3-membered cyclic bromonium ion.

questions.question: What is the transition state geometry in the hydroboration of an alkene by BH₃·THF?

options.label: A
options.text: A radical pair transition state with homolytic B-H cleavage.

options.label: B
options.text: A linear two-step ionic transition state involving a free carbocation.

options.label: C
options.text: A concerted, four-centered square planar transition state where boron adds to the less hindered carbon and hydrogen adds simultaneously to the more substituted carbon on the same face.

options.label: D
options.text: A six-membered cyclic transition state involving two borane molecules.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted, four-centered square planar transition state where boron adds to the less hindered carbon and hydrogen adds simultaneously to the more substituted carbon on the same face.
questions.explanation: Hydroboration is a concerted syn-addition with a 4-membered transition state directed by steric and electronic stabilization.

questions.question: Why does oxymercuration of 3,3-dimethyl-1-butene yield the Markovnikov alcohol without carbocation rearrangement?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an SN2 displacement on mercury.

options.label: B
options.text: The reaction proceeds through a bridged mercurinium ion intermediate, which prevents the open carbocation from undergoing 1,2-hydride or methyl shifts.

options.label: C
options.text: Mercuric acetate acts as a strong radical scavenger.

options.label: D
options.text: Water attacks the double bond before mercury coordinates.

questions.correct_answer: The reaction proceeds through a bridged mercurinium ion intermediate, which prevents the open carbocation from undergoing 1,2-hydride or methyl shifts.
questions.explanation: Bridged mercurinium ions delocalize charge and prevent skeletal carbocation rearrangements.

questions.question: What is the first elementary step in the dihydroxylation of alkenes by KMnO₄ or OsO₄?

options.label: A
options.text: Proton transfer from the metal to the alkene.

options.label: B
options.text: An SN2 backside attack by hydroxide ion.

options.label: C
options.text: A concerted [3+2] pericyclic cycloaddition of the metal oxo groups across the alkene π bond to form a cyclic metallate ester.

options.label: D
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the metal-oxygen double bond.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted [3+2] pericyclic cycloaddition of the metal oxo groups across the alkene π bond to form a cyclic metallate ester.
questions.explanation: Concerted [3+2] cycloaddition delivers both oxygen atoms to the same face of the alkene simultaneously, guaranteeing syn stereochemistry.

questions.question: What is the sequence of mechanistic steps in the conversion of an alkene to a trans-1,2-diol using mCPBA followed by aqueous acid?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the alkene π bond by peroxide radicals.

options.label: B
options.text: Ozonolysis followed by zinc reduction.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct syn addition of two OH groups followed by a ring flip.

options.label: D
options.text: Concerted epoxidation of the alkene, protonation of the epoxide oxygen, and backside nucleophilic attack by water with inversion of configuration.

questions.correct_answer: Concerted epoxidation of the alkene, protonation of the epoxide oxygen, and backside nucleophilic attack by water with inversion of configuration.
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed epoxide ring opening involves backside nucleophilic attack by water, inverting one stereocenter to deliver the trans-diol.

questions.question: What is the initial unstable adduct formed when ozone reacts with an alkene at -78°C?

options.label: A
options.text: A stable 1,2-dioxetane four-membered ring.

options.label: B
options.text: A secondary ozonide directly without fragmentation.

options.label: C
options.text: A bis-epoxide intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: A primary ozonide (molozonide) formed by [3+2] cycloaddition, which rapidly fragments into a carbonyl compound and a carbonyl oxide (Criegee zwitterion).

questions.correct_answer: A primary ozonide (molozonide) formed by [3+2] cycloaddition, which rapidly fragments into a carbonyl compound and a carbonyl oxide (Criegee zwitterion).
questions.explanation: The initially formed molozonide undergoes retro-[3+2] cleavage and recombines into the more stable secondary ozonide.

questions.question: In the peroxide-promoted addition of HBr to alkenes, what is the structure of the radical intermediate?

options.label: A
options.text: A bromine-centered radical on the tertiary carbon.

options.label: B
options.text: A carbon-centered radical located on the more substituted carbon, formed when the bromine radical (Br•) adds to the terminal alkene carbon.

options.label: C
options.text: A primary carbocation intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: A cyclic bromonium radical cation.

questions.correct_answer: A carbon-centered radical located on the more substituted carbon, formed when the bromine radical (Br•) adds to the terminal alkene carbon.
questions.explanation: Bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon to generate the more stable, highly substituted secondary or tertiary carbon radical.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic pathway for catalytic alkene hydrogenation over a palladium surface?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction proceeds via hydride radicals in homogeneous solution.

options.label: B
options.text: Palladium ionizes the alkene into a dication.

options.label: C
options.text: Hydrogen gas directly inserts into C=C in the gas phase without metal contact.

options.label: D
options.text: Hydrogen molecules dissociate homolytically into surface-bound H atoms; the alkene coordinates via its π bond and receives two hydrogens sequentially on the same face (syn).

questions.correct_answer: Hydrogen molecules dissociate homolytically into surface-bound H atoms; the alkene coordinates via its π bond and receives two hydrogens sequentially on the same face (syn).
